subject: Cross-cloud marketplace fee recalibration proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Amir Patel <amir.patel@cloudbridge.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: jill.huang@amazon.com, listings@azurepartners.net
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: blended listing credit to offset FY27 marketplace fees

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. Per our conversation, CloudBridge (we run the partner finance program for AWS/GCP/Azure listings) put together an initial proposal to reduce Redwood's effective listing drag for FY27 across all three clouds. The attached spreadsheet has the numbers, but high level:

- Introduce a blended listing credit equal to 60% of first-year listing fees for customers procured via marketplace channels, payable as a quarterly rebate against invoices.
- Tie the credit to a 12-month commit and 3-month ramp; if Redwood meets the ramp targets we guarantee the credit for the remainder of FY27.
- Offer an additional co-marketing fund ($75k) if Redwood hits $1.2M ARR through marketplace listings within 9 months.

What we'd like from your side: a short confirmation that Redwood can accept a quarterly rebate structure (rather than an upfront invoice offset), and any procurement/legal constraints we should be aware of (PO timing, invoicing address, etc.).

Attachment: cross_cloud_fee_proposal.xlsx (spreadsheet, 23KB)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the numbers.

—Amir
Head of Partner Finance, CloudBridge
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Amir Patel <amir.patel@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-30T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: blended listing credit to offset FY27 marketplace fees

Amir —

Appreciate the clear proposal. Quick notes from Redwood:

- Procurement: Quarterly rebate is workable but we need the credit spelled out in the SOW/MPA so finance can apply it to invoices. PO lifecycle is typically 30 days after SOW countersignature.
- Finance: rishi (cc'd) will confirm whether rebate can be applied as an invoice credit vs. separate payment.
- Marketing/GTN: the $75k co-marketing fund is attractive; we need clarity on eligible spend and co-branding terms.

I'd like to loop in Ben from Partnerships (ben_carter) and Legal to review the attached term changes. Can you share a short bullet summary in the spreadsheet of what triggers the credit and the audit evidence you expect?

Proposed next step: 30-min call with Amir, Jill (AWS), GCP listings rep, Ben, Rishi, and me on Tuesday 9/1 at 10am PT. Are you and the cloud teams available?

—Marissa
Sr. Partnerships Lead, Redwood Inference
From: jill.huang@amazon.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Amir Patel <amir.patel@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-01T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: blended listing credit to offset FY27 marketplace fees

Marissa / Amir —

Thanks for the invite. AWS can join Tuesday 9/1 at 10am PT (confirmed). A few clarifications ahead of the call so we can be prepared:

1) AWS typically requires credits tied to verified transactable usage that we can reconcile via our marketplace reporting. Are you proposing the credit based on redemptions through the marketplace listing, or on gross bookings attributable to Marketplace-led deals?
2) Auditability: we will need the contract to allow access to relevant metrics or a monthly report feed.
3) Term and clawback: what language does CloudBridge expect around retroactive clawbacks if revenue cannot be verified?

We can discuss these on the call; please send any sample language or the short bullet summary Marissa requested.

—Jill
AWS Marketplace Partner Lead
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Amir Patel <amir.patel@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-01T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: blended listing credit to offset FY27 marketplace fees

Amir / team —

I reviewed the spreadsheet. From Finance: quarterly rebate via credit memo is acceptable, but we need:

- A single master rebate schedule attached to the PO/SOW with exact calculation (gross bookings via marketplace * credit rate).
- Definitional clarity: what constitutes a "marketplace-led" order (checkout vs. referral). We prefer marketplace transactable orders only for simple reconciliation.
- Standard audit window: 90 days post-quarter to submit disputes/evidence.

If CloudBridge and the clouds are open to transactable-only credits (i.e., purchases that flow through the marketplace checkout), we can move fast. If you're tying credits to referred/attributed bookings, legal will need to review attribution methodology.

Also copying Ben to confirm Partnerships OK with the $75k GTM fund mechanics.

—Rishi
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Amir Patel <amir.patel@cloudbridge.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, jill.huang@amazon.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-02T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: blended listing credit to offset FY27 marketplace fees

Thanks all — good discussion on the call. Follow-ups and proposed commitments: 

- CloudBridge confirms that the proposed credit will be scoped to transactable marketplace orders (checkout flows) by default. We'll include a separate appendix for referral-attribution credits if Redwood wants hybrid coverage.
- We'll draft a concise rebate schedule and sample language for inclusion in the MPA/SOW (will attach a redline of Redwood-marketplace-terms-diff.docx).
- For the $75k co-marketing fund: it will be remitted after Redwood submits eligible GTM invoices and co-branding assets; CloudBridge will reimburse up to $75k within 60 days of invoice acceptance.
- Reporting: CloudBridge will provide a monthly CSV export for reconciliation; audit window 90 days.

Next steps: Amir to share draft appendix + rebate schedule by 9/4. Redwood to confirm whether you want the referral appendix included in the SOW or handled as a separate bilateral addendum.

Attachment: redwood_marketplace_terms-diff.docx (word doc, 18KB)

We can iterate the language quickly — aiming for countersign by end of September if possible.

—Amir
